## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

     9→  _ulid: UlidSchema,

    11→  created_at: DateTimeSchema,
    12→  tags: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
    13→  added_by: z.string().optional(), // e.g., "@claude", "alice"
    14→});
    15→
    16→/**
    17→ * Inbox item input schema (for creating new items)
    18→ */
    19→export const InboxItemInputSchema = z.object({
    20→  _ulid: UlidSchema.optional(),
    21→  text: z.string().min(1, "Text is required"),
    22→  created_at: DateTimeSchema.optional(),
    23→  tags: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
    24→  added_by: z.string().optional(),
    25→});
    26→
    27→/**

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

/**
 * Field labels and section headers used throughout the CLI output
 */

import chalk from "chalk";

/**
 * Session context section headers
 */
export const sessionHeaders = {
  title: chalk.blue.bold("=== Session Context ==="),
  activeWork: chalk.cyan.bold("--- Active Work ---"),
  noActiveWork: chalk.gray("--- No Active Work ---"),
  awaitingReview: chalk.yellow.bold("--- Awaiting Review ---"),
  recentlyCompleted: chalk.green.bold("--- Recently Completed ---"),
  recentActivity: chalk.cyan.bold("--- Recent Activity ---"),
  recentNotes: chalk.cyan.bold("--- Recent Notes ---"),
  incompleteTodos: chalk.yellow.bold("--- Incomplete Todos ---"),
  readyTasks: chalk.cyan.bold("--- Ready to Pick Up ---"),
  blocked: chalk.red.bold("--- Blocked ---"),
  recentCommits: chalk.cyan.bold("--- Recent Commits ---"),
  inbox: chalk.magenta.bold("--- Inbox (oldest first) ---"),
  workingTree: chalk.yellow.bold("--- Working Tree ---"),
  workingTreeClean: chalk.gray("--- Working Tree: Clean ---"),
  quickCommands: chalk.gray.bold("--- Quick Commands ---"),
} as const;

/**
 * Task/Item detail field labels
 */
export const fieldLabels = {
  ulid: "ULID:",
  slugs: "Slugs:",
  title: "Title:",
  type: "Type:",
  status: "Status:",
  priority: "Priority:",
  automation: "Automation:",
  maturity: "Maturity:",
  specRef: "Spec ref:",
  metaRef: "Meta ref:",
  depends: "Depends:",
  blocked: "Blocked:",
  dependsOn: "Depends on:",
  implements: "Implements:",
  relatesTo: "Relates to:",
  tags: "Tags:",
  created: "Created:",
  started: "Started:",
  completed: "Completed:",
  implementation: "Implementation: ",
  description: "Description:",
  acceptanceCriteria: "Acceptance Criteria:",
  traceability: "Traceability:",
} as const;

/**
 * Output section separators
 */
export const sectionHeaders = {
  specContext: chalk.gray("─── Spec Context ───"),
  description: chalk.gray("─── Description ───"),
  acceptanceCriteria: chalk.gray("─── Acceptance Criteria ───"),
  notes: chalk.gray("─── Notes ───"),
  todos: chalk.gray("─── Todos ───"),
} as const;

/**
 * Common CLI hints/suggestions
 */
export const hints = {
  inboxPromote: chalk.gray("Use: kspec inbox promote <ref> to convert to task"),
  inboxTriage: chalk.gray(
    "Use: kspec triage inbox to triage untriaged items",
  ),
  taskNote: (ref: string) =>
    chalk.gray(`Use: kspec task note ${ref} "<note>" to add context`),
  taskComplete: (ref: string) =>
    chalk.gray(
      `Use: kspec task complete ${ref} --reason "<summary>" when done`,
    ),
  taskStart: (ref: string) =>
    chalk.gray(`Use: kspec task start ${ref} to begin work`),
  gitCommit: chalk.gray(
    'Use: git add -A && git commit -m "..." to commit changes',
  ),
} as const;

/**
 * Summary/count messages
 */
export const summaries = {
  noTasks: chalk.gray("No tasks found"),
  taskCount: (count: number) => chalk.gray(`${count} task(s)`),
} as const;

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

    status:
      maturity: draft
      implementation: implemented
    priority: high
    tags:
      - mvp
      - cli
    description: |
      The CLI is designed for both human and agent use.
      Consistent structure, predictable output, clear errors.
    requirements:
      - _ulid: 01KEZCJPHWP32HK8MR38P2WSSJ
        slugs:
          - cli-structure
        title: Command Structure
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: verified
        description: |
          Commands follow consistent structure:

          kspec <resource> <action> [args] [flags]

          Resources: item, task, link, todo, etc.
          Actions: add, get, list, set, delete, etc.

          Examples:
          - kspec item add --type feature --title "Login"
          - kspec task start @impl-login
          - kspec tasks ready
        implements:
          - "@cli-design"
      - _ulid: 01KEZCJPHWKVBFSAEP0MMH57DQ
        slugs:
          - cli-json-output
        title: JSON Output Mode
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: verified
        description: |
          All commands support --json flag for structured output:

          kspec tasks ready --json
          kspec item get @login --json

          JSON output includes:
          - success: boolean
          - data: The result
          - errors: Array of error objects (if any)
        implements:
          - "@cli-design"
      - _ulid: 01KEZCJPHWB81SAWT4ZGCV75FC
        slugs:
          - cli-exit-codes
        title: Semantic Exit Codes
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: implemented
        description: |
          Exit codes are semantic, not just 0/1:

          - 0: Success
          - 1: General error
          - 2: Usage error (bad arguments)
          - 3: Not found
          - 4: Validation failed
          - 5: Conflict (already exists, etc.)

          Scripts can handle specific cases.
        implements:
          - "@cli-design"
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: exit-code-constants
            given: CLI codebase uses exit codes
            when: Commands need to exit with specific code
            then: Uses named constants from a centralized EXIT_CODES object (e.g., EXIT_CODES.NOT_FOUND instead
              of magic number 3)
          - id: exit-codes-documented
            given: User wants to script kspec commands
            when: User runs kspec help --exit-codes or checks documentation
            then: All exit codes are listed with their meanings and which commands may return them
          - id: consistent-usage
            given: Multiple commands use exit codes
            when: Commands exit with errors
            then: All commands use consistent exit codes for the same error types (e.g., all 'not found' errors
              exit 3, all validation errors exit 4)
        notes:
          - _ulid: 01KFADD1NW999DBZJHBDBSPFZM
            created_at: 2026-01-19T05:59:47.645Z
            author: "@claude"
            content: >-
              Enhancement: Formalize exit code implementation


              **Current state:** Exit codes are defined in spec but implementation uses magic
              numbers inconsistently.


              **Goals:**

              1. Centralized constants - single source of truth

              2. Documentation - help users script with kspec

              3. Consistency audit - ensure all commands follow the spec


              **Exit code definitions (from spec):**

              - 0: SUCCESS - Operation completed successfully

              - 1: ERROR - General/unexpected error

              - 2: USAGE - Bad arguments, invalid command usage

              - 3: NOT_FOUND - Referenced item doesn't exist

              - 4: VALIDATION - Spec validation failed

              - 5: CONFLICT - Item already exists, duplicate slug, etc.


              **New additions to consider:**

              - 6: PARTIAL - Some operations succeeded, some failed (for batch operations)


              **Documentation format:** Add to 'kspec help' or new 'kspec help --exit-codes'
              subcommand showing all codes with descriptions.
            supersedes: null
      - _ulid: 01KEZCJPHWBEEP2BYRP6YVNK9F
        slugs:
          - cli-agent-features
        title: Agent-Friendly Features
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: verified
        description: |
          Features for agent/script usage:

          - --json: Structured output
          - --no-prompt: Never prompt (KSPEC_NO_PROMPT=1)
          - --dry-run: Show what would happen
          - --if-not-exists: Idempotent creation
          - --quiet: Suppress non-essential output

          Agents should be able to use kspec without interaction.
        implements:
          - "@cli-design"
        requirements:
          - _ulid: 01KHA83NH88Q21QF947XXRDRBE
            slugs:
              - output-format-option
            title: Output Format Option
            type: requirement
            tags: []
            description: |
              Add a --format <json|yaml> global option with --json, --raw, and --yaml as
              shorthands. Agents frequently try --raw and --yaml flags expecting structured
              output. --raw is a shorthand for --format json (agents associate raw with
              give me the data). --yaml is a shorthand for --format yaml. --json remains
              as a shorthand for --format json. The --format option is extensible for
              future formats. This replaces the precedence model in @trait-json-output
              ac-6 with explicit format selection.
            acceptance_criteria:
              - id: ac-format-json
                given: User runs any command with --format json
                when: The format option is set to json
                then: Output is identical to current --json behavior
              - id: ac-format-yaml
                given: User runs any command with --format yaml
                when: The format option is set to yaml
                then: Output contains the same data as --json but serialized as valid YAML
              - id: ac-json-shorthand
                given: User runs any command with --json
                when: The --json shorthand is used
                then: Equivalent to --format json (backward compatible, existing behavior preserved)
              - id: ac-raw-shorthand
                given: User runs any command with --raw
                when: The --raw shorthand is used
                then: Equivalent to --format json (same data, JSON serialization)
              - id: ac-yaml-shorthand
                given: User runs any command with --yaml
                when: The --yaml shorthand is used
                then: Equivalent to --format yaml
              - id: ac-conflict-error
                given: User runs a command with conflicting format options (e.g. --json --yaml)
                when: Multiple format specifications are provided
                then: Error message explains the conflict and exits non-zero
              - id: ac-yaml-no-ansi
                given: User runs any command with --format yaml
                when: YAML output is generated
                then: Output contains no ANSI escape codes (same contract as --json)
              - id: ac-yaml-references
                given: User runs kspec task get @ref --yaml
                when: Output contains reference fields
                then: References include @ prefix (same contract as --json)
              - id: ac-global-scope
                given: User runs any command that supports structured output with --format, --yaml, or --raw
                when: The option is used on any command
                then: The option works globally (same scope as --json)
              - id: ac-unsupported-format
                given: User runs --format csv or another unsupported format name
                when: An invalid format value is provided
                then: Error message lists valid formats (json, yaml) and exits non-zero
            depends_on: []
            implements: []
            relates_to: []
            tests: []
            traits:

              - "@trait-semantic-exit-codes"
            notes: []

        slugs:

        description: The CLI must display the correct version from package.json when running 'kspec
          --version' or 'kspec -V'. Version must stay in sync with the npm package version.
        depends_on: []

        created: 2026-01-22T04:35:53.841Z
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: kspec is installed from npm
            when: user runs 'kspec --version' or 'kspec -V'
            then: displays the version from package.json (e.g., '0.1.1')
          - id: ac-2
            given: a new version is released
            when: package.json version is updated
            then: CLI --version output automatically reflects the new version without code changes
          - id: ac-3
            given: kspec is run in development via 'npm run dev'
            when: user runs 'npm run dev -- --version'
            then: displays the same version as package.json
        status:
          maturity: draft

        notes: []

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: kspec session start

Display session context for starting work. Two output modes: primer (default) shows curated actionable data; full (--full) shows same structure with more items and additional sections. Sections ordered by actionability. Empty sections omitted. Task refs display as @slug in human output (fallback to @short-ulid). Timestamps relative in human output, ISO 8601 in JSON.

Acceptance Criteria (15):
  [ac-primer-default]
    Given: no format flags specified
    When: kspec session start runs
    Then: primer mode renders: header, active tasks, pending review, blocked, ready (top 5), recent activity (10 items), inbox stat line, working tree (if dirty), quick commands
  [ac-full-sections]
    Given: --full flag passed
    When: output renders
    Then: same section ordering as primer plus: all ready tasks, 20 activity items, up to 20 untriaged inbox items, observations section, session metadata (if populated)
  [ac-brief-alias]
    Given: --brief flag passed
    When: output renders
    Then: behaves identically to primer (backward-compat no-op alias)
  [ac-section-order]
    Given: multiple sections have data
    When: output renders
    Then: rendered sections appear in order: active tasks, pending review, blocked, ready, recent activity, inbox, working tree, quick commands
  [ac-empty-skip]
    Given: a section has zero items
    When: output renders
    Then: that section is omitted entirely (no header, no placeholder message)
  [ac-slug-display]
    Given: task has slugs
    When: human output renders
    Then: task ref displays as @slug
  [ac-slug-fallback]
    Given: task has no slugs or item is inbox (no slug schema)
    When: human output renders
    Then: ref displays as @short-ulid
  [ac-relative-time-human]
    Given: items have timestamps
    When: human output renders
    Then: all times shown as relative (2h ago, 3d ago)
  [ac-iso-time-json]
    Given: --json flag used
    When: JSON output renders
    Then: all timestamps remain ISO 8601
  [ac-dirty-tree-only]
    Given: working tree is clean
    When: output renders
    Then: working tree section omitted
  [ac-active-detail]
    Given: tasks are in_progress or needs_work
    When: primer or full renders
    Then: shows title, description, and recent notes (richest detail level)
  [ac-needs-work-indicator]
    Given: task status is needs_work
    When: output renders
    Then: visually distinguished from in_progress with status label
  [ac-review-detail]
    Given: tasks are pending_review
    When: primer or full renders
    Then: shows title and recent notes
  [ac-notes-starvation]
    Given: tasks in multiple statuses have notes
    When: notes render
    Then: notes split across statuses to prevent starvation (in_progress, pending_review, completed each get fair share)
  [ac-json-raw-preserved]
    Given: --json flag used
    When: JSON output renders
    Then: existing recently_completed and recent_commits arrays present and unchanged

# PR #516 Review

## Findings

1. MUST-FIX — `@trait-json-output ac-4` is asserted with the opposite expectation of the current trait spec.
   - `kspec item get @cmd-session-start` still inherits `@trait-json-output ac-4` as: "references use @ prefix consistently".
   - The new test at `tests/cli/session-start-format.test.ts` asserts `task.ref` is a bare 8-char ULID and documents JSON refs as identifiers without `@`.
   - This makes the AC annotation misleading and will lock in behavior that contradicts the trait unless the trait/spec is updated in the same PR.

2. SHOULD-FIX — `@trait-semantic-exit-codes ac-5` coverage is too weak / mislabeled.
   - The new test is annotated as "exit 0 with empty result set" but does not create or verify an empty-result scenario.
   - It explicitly notes the fixture may already contain data and only checks that arrays exist, which overlaps with general success-path coverage (`ac-1`) rather than `ac-5`.

3. SHOULD-FIX — new human-output tests for `@session-start-activity-timeline` ACs do not assert the visual requirements in the AC text.
   - `ac-activity-hierarchy` requires linked commits to appear nested beneath task entries with a visual connector.
   - `ac-activity-orphan` requires standalone indented entries visually distinct from task entries.
   - The added assertions mostly check string presence / task-title absence, but not indentation/connector/line structure.

## Checks Run

- `gh pr diff 516`
- `gh pr view 516 --json title,body,files`
- `kspec task get @task-session-start-output-tests`
- `kspec item get @cmd-session-start`
- `kspec item get @session-start-activity-timeline --json`
- `kspec validate` (fails due unrelated repo-wide duplicate `@observations` refs and existing alignment/completeness warnings)
- `pnpm vitest run tests/cli/session-start-activity-timeline.test.ts tests/cli/session-start-format.test.ts tests/cli/session-start-notes.test.ts` (72 tests passed)

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

Ralph max-tasks-per-iteration limiting
Type: requirement
Implementation: implemented
Description:
  Limits how many tasks can be completed per iteration via --max-tasks flag. Default is 1 (conservative), 0 means unlimited. Enforcement is soft (message injection) then hard (PreToolUse hook blocking task start). Counts kspec task complete AND kspec task submit commands (submit transitions to pending_review, meaning the agent's work is done).
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-flag]
    Given: User runs kspec ralph
    When: --max-tasks flag is provided or defaults
    Then: Parses N as positive integer (1-999) or 0 for unlimited; default is 1; invalid values exit with code 2
  [ac-detection]
    Given: Agent completes or submits a task (kspec task complete or kspec task submit)
    When: ACP update handler receives Bash tool call containing kspec task complete or kspec task submit
    Then: Ralph queries kspec for actual completion count since iteration start, counting both completed and pending_review tasks, not relying on pattern alone
  [ac-wrapup]
    Given: N tasks completed this iteration (N equals max-tasks)
    When: Detection triggers and count verified via kspec query
    Then: Ralph writes marker file and injects wrap-up message telling agent to stop starting new tasks
  [ac-unlimited]
    Given: --max-tasks 0 is specified
    When: Ralph runs iteration
    Then: No task limit enforced (legacy behavior); no marker file written
  [ac-hook-block]
    Given: Marker file exists at .claude/ralph-task-limit.json with active:true
    When: PreToolUse hook intercepts kspec task start command
    Then: Hook blocks with message explaining task limit reached; allows other commands
  [ac-reset]
    Given: New iteration begins
    When: Ralph starts iteration loop
    Then: Counter resets to 0; stale marker files older than 1 hour are cleared
  [ac-marker-format]
    Given: Task limit reached
    When: Marker file written
    Then: File is JSON with active, since (ISO8601), max, completed, sessionId fields
  [ac-dryrun]
    Given: --dry-run flag provided with --max-tasks N
    When: Ralph shows config
    Then: Displays max-tasks configuration in dry-run output
  [ac-signal-cleanup]
    Given: Ralph is running with an active task-limit marker file
    When: The process receives SIGINT (Ctrl+C) or SIGTERM
    Then: The marker file is cleaned up before the process exits, cross-platform

─── Notes ───
[2026-02-25T00:36:01.762Z] @claude:
Bug: ralph signal handler (src/cli/commands/ralph.ts ~lines 1057-1071) queues Promise.all for fs.unlink(budget) + closeSession() but does not await it — process.exit(0) in .finally() fires before I/O completes. This causes budget.json to persist after SIGINT, failing ac-signal-cleanup.

Root cause: fire-and-forget async cleanup in synchronous signal handler. The normal exit path (finally block ~line 1513) correctly awaits the same cleanup.

Fix: await cleanup promises before calling process.exit(). Either use async handler pattern or set a flag and let the event loop drain. Only one instance of this pattern exists — no other signal handlers in the codebase have this issue.

rawInput.command: kspec task note @01KJ93JJ "Fixed unawaited async cleanup in ralph signal handler. The signalCleanup function created Promise.all() for budget deletion + session close but never awaited it — process.exit(0) in .finally() fired before I/O completed. Changed to async IIFE pattern: void (async () => { try { await Promise.all([...]); } catch {} finally { process.exit(0); } })(). Updated static analysis test in end-loop.test.ts to match new pattern. Added AC annotation for @ralph-task-limit ac-signal-cleanup to both SIGINT and SIGTERM signal tests. All tests pass."

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

        acceptance_criteria:

            given: |
              completed tasks and git commits exist
            when: |
              recent activity section renders
            then: |
              both sources appear in a single chronological list
          - id: ac-activity-trailer-link
            given: |
              a commit has Task: @slug trailer in its body
            when: |
              recent activity renders
            then: |
              that commit shows linked task info alongside it
          - id: ac-activity-sort
            given: |
              activity items have mixed timestamps
            when: |
              timeline renders

              sorted chronologically
          - id: ac-activity-dedup
            given: "multiple commits are linked to the same task via Task: @slug trailers"
            when: |
              timeline renders
            then: commits are grouped under a single task entry as nested children, not shown as separate
              top-level entries
          - id: ac-activity-no-git
            given: |
              --no-git flag is passed
            when: |
              activity timeline renders
            then: |
              only task completions shown, no commit entries
          - id: ac-activity-hierarchy
            given: linked commits and completed tasks exist
            when: human-readable timeline renders
            then: tasks are top-level entries and linked commits appear nested beneath their task with a visual

          - id: ac-activity-orphan
            given: "a commit has no Task: @slug trailer"
            when: human-readable timeline renders

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

Acceptance Criteria (9):
  [ac-flag]

    Then: Parses N as positive integer (1-999) or 0 for unlimited; default is 1; invalid values exit with code 2
  [ac-detection]
    Given: Agent completes or submits a task (kspec task complete or kspec task submit)
    When: ACP update handler receives Bash tool call containing kspec task complete or kspec task submit
    Then: Ralph queries kspec for actual completion count since iteration start, counting both completed and pending_review tasks, not relying on pattern alone
  [ac-wrapup]
    Given: N tasks completed this iteration (N equals max-tasks)
    When: Detection triggers and count verified via kspec query
    Then: Ralph writes marker file and injects wrap-up message telling agent to stop starting new tasks
  [ac-unlimited]
    Given: --max-tasks 0 is specified
    When: Ralph runs iteration
    Then: No task limit enforced (legacy behavior); no marker file written
  [ac-hook-block]
    Given: Marker file exists at .claude/ralph-task-limit.json with active:true

  [ac-reset]

    When: Ralph starts iteration loop
    Then: Counter resets to 0; stale marker files older than 1 hour are cleared
  [ac-marker-format]
    Given: Task limit reached
    When: Marker file written
    Then: File is JSON with active, since (ISO8601), max, completed, sessionId fields
  [ac-dryrun]
    Given: --dry-run flag provided with --max-tasks N
    When: Ralph shows config
    Then: Displays max-tasks configuration in dry-run output
  [ac-signal-cleanup]
    Given: Ralph is running with an active task-limit marker file

Ralph max-tasks-per-iteration limiting
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KG6CHDCEB2D34NEDF1QSWW80
Slugs:     ralph-task-limit
Type:      requirement
Maturity:  draft
Implementation: in_progress

─── Description ───
Limits how many tasks can be completed per iteration via --max-tasks flag. Default is 1 (conservative), 0 means unlimited. Enforcement is soft (message injection) then hard (PreToolUse hook blocking task start). Counts kspec task complete AND kspec task submit commands (submit transitions to pending_review, meaning the agent's work is done).

─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-flag]
    Given: User runs kspec ralph
    When: --max-tasks flag is provided or defaults
    Then: Parses N as positive integer (1-999) or 0 for unlimited; default is 1; invalid values exit with code 2
  [ac-detection]
    Given: Agent completes or submits a task (kspec task complete or kspec task submit)
    When: ACP update handler receives Bash tool call containing kspec task complete or kspec task submit
    Then: Ralph queries kspec for actual completion count since iteration start, counting both completed and pending_review tasks, not relying on pattern alone
  [ac-wrapup]
    Given: N tasks completed this iteration (N equals max-tasks)
    When: Detection triggers and count verified via kspec query
    Then: Ralph writes marker file and injects wrap-up message telling agent to stop starting new tasks
  [ac-unlimited]
    Given: --max-tasks 0 is specified
    When: Ralph runs iteration
    Then: No task limit enforced (legacy behavior); no marker file written
  [ac-hook-block]
    Given: Marker file exists at .claude/ralph-task-limit.json with active:true
    When: PreToolUse hook intercepts kspec task start command
    Then: Hook blocks with message explaining task limit reached; allows other commands
  [ac-reset]
    Given: New iteration begins
    When: Ralph starts iteration loop
    Then: Counter resets to 0; stale marker files older than 1 hour are cleared
  [ac-marker-format]
    Given: Task limit reached
    When: Marker file written
    Then: File is JSON with active, since (ISO8601), max, completed, sessionId fields
  [ac-dryrun]
    Given: --dry-run flag provided with --max-tasks N
    When: Ralph shows config
    Then: Displays max-tasks configuration in dry-run output
  [ac-signal-cleanup]
    Given: Ralph is running with an active task-limit marker file
    When: The process receives SIGINT (Ctrl+C) or SIGTERM
    Then: The marker file is cleaned up before the process exits, cross-platform

ULID:      01KJ6KKPPYCDDBPV7MZZ9P21ZF
Slugs:     ralph-session-budget-integration
Type:      feature
Maturity:  draft
Implementation: implemented

─── Description ───
Integrate session budget into the ralph loop, replacing marker file management
and ACP output parsing for task completion detection. Ralph creates sessions with
budget, resets budget per iteration, and passes KSPEC_SESSION_ID to spawned agents.
Major simplification of the ralph main loop. Also removes end-loop marker logic
in favor of session-scoped end-loop signal.


─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-create-budget]
    Given: ralph starts a loop with --max-tasks N

    When: it creates the session

    Then: budget.json is written with max_per_cycle=N in the session directory

  [ac-reset-iteration]
    Given: ralph starts a new iteration

    When: it prepares the iteration context (agent is not running)

    Then: it calls resetBudget() to set started_this_cycle=0

  [ac-env-inject]
    Given: ralph spawns an agent for an iteration

    When: the agent process starts

    Then: KSPEC_SESSION_ID is set in the agent's environment variables

  [ac-remove-marker-code]
    Given: budget and end-loop enforcement is session-scoped

    When: ralph runs

    Then: all marker file code (task-limit and end-loop), detectTaskCompleteCommand,
and ACP prompt injection for task limits are removed from ralph.ts

  [ac-session-close-all-paths]
    Given: the ralph loop ends for any reason (normal exit, no tasks, max failures,
SIGINT, SIGTERM, uncaught error)

    When: cleanup runs

    Then: session status is updated (completed for normal, abandoned for error/signal)
and budget.json is cleaned up

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

feat: Feature description

Task: @task-slug
Spec: @spec-ref
```

Trailers enable `kspec log @ref` to find commits by task or spec.

Link tests to acceptance criteria using language-appropriate comment syntax:

```javascript
// AC: @spec-item ac-N
it('should validate input', () => { ... });
```

```python
# AC: @spec-item ac-N
def test_validates_input():
    ...
```

## Commit Convention

```
feat: Feature description

Task: @task-slug
Spec: @spec-ref
```

Trailers enable `kspec log @ref` to find commits by task or spec.

## Code Annotations

Link tests to acceptance criteria using language-appropriate comment syntax:

```javascript
// AC: @spec-item ac-N
it('should validate input', () => { ... });
```

```python
# AC: @spec-item ac-N
def test_validates_input():
    ...
```

Every AC SHOULD have at least one test with this annotation.

### N/A Trait ACs

When a trait AC doesn't apply to a specific spec, annotate it as N/A with a reason:

```javascript
// AC: @trait-slug ac-N — N/A: reason why it doesn't apply
```

Group N/A annotations together in a dedicated test or at the top of the test file. The `// AC:` prefix is required — do not use prose comments or bullet lists. The annotation must be machine-parseable.

## Code Annotations

Link tests to acceptance criteria using language-appropriate comment syntax:

### N/A Trait ACs

When a trait AC doesn't apply to a specific spec, annotate it as N/A with a reason:

```javascript
// AC: @trait-slug ac-N — N/A: reason why it doesn't apply
```
